correctness.rationale: Convex vertex sets in trees are connected subtrees. A bipartition into two connected parts crosses exactly one edge; conversely each edge cut is convex on both sides. Three noncollinear terminals have a median outside their triple, making each singleton and complement realizable by a branch cut. If one terminal lies between two others, convexity forbids selecting endpoints but omitting middle. On four terminals compatible tree splits cannot realize all crossing 2-versus-2 labelings. Collinear triples correspond bijectively to interior vertices of each endpoint path, counted by W(T)-C(n,2). Star/path bounds follow edge-cut distance contributions. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 1442 Prüfer-labeled trees n<=6 verified the profile and split characterization. Exhaustive small n alone does not prove arbitrary trees.

final_claim: For any finite nonempty simple tree, geodesic halfspaces with convex complements are the two trivial sets and two oriented edge-cut components per edge. All supports of size<=2 and exactly noncollinear triples are shattered; none larger. The profile is 1+nz+C(n,2)z²+[C(n,3)+C(n,2)-W(T)]z³, so Wiener index is recovered and VC dimension is 1 on singleton, 2 on nontrivial paths, 3 on other trees.
